slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌
content_zh:
第五十一章千机
月光照在山坡上，银白的光把整片墓地照得一清二楚。苏尘和铁兴没有回头，踩着野草和碎石往下走。身后的石壁在月光下越来越远，最后被山坡的起伏遮住了，再也看不见了。
脚下没有路。
都是野草和碎石，走一步滑半步，时不时踩到一块松动的石头，石头滚下去，在寂静的夜里发出一连串的声响。苏尘尽量挑草密的地方走——草密的地方土实一些，不容易滑。铁兴跟在他身后，步子比他重一些，每踩一步都能听到石子被碾进土里的声响。
下了那道坡，前面是一片更密的山林。树木不高，但很密——松树、柞木、灌木丛，乱七八糟地长在一起，枝桠交缠着，在月光下投出一片一片的黑影。地上的落叶积得很厚，踩上去软绵绵的，散发出一股潮湿的腐木气味。
苏尘站在林子的边缘，回头看了一眼。
山坡上那面石壁已经看不到了。整片山坡在月光下安安静静的，只有风从草尖上吹过去的声音。
铁兴站在他旁边，也回头看了一眼。他的呼吸还没完全平下来，胸口一起一伏的。
“我们真出来了。”他说。语气里带着一种不真实的感，像是还在确认自己不是在做梦。
“还没出去。”苏尘说，“只是从山洞里出来了。还在人家的地盘上。”
铁兴想了想，点了点头。
“往哪走？”他问。
苏尘抬头看了看月亮的位置。他在山洞里关了好几天，不知道外面的方向，但月亮的方向总归是差不多的。他指了指西北方向——那边山势看起来更低一些，树也稀疏一些，应该能翻过去。
“那边。”
两个人没有再多说，踩着落叶，钻进林子里去了。
——
从墓地翻出来之后的第一夜，两个人几乎没睡。
不是不想睡——是根本找不到一个能踏实躺下的地方。林子里的地面不平，到处都是凸起的树根和埋在落叶底下的石头，坐下去硌得慌，躺下去更硌。而且夜里的山风冷，从林子的缝隙里吹进来，带着水汽，很快就把衣服吹透了。
苏尘找了一棵大松树，树干粗壮，树冠撑开像一个伞盖，把月光和夜风都挡掉了大半。他在树根旁边蹲下来，用手扒开地面的落叶——落叶底下是湿土，带着一股浓重的泥土腥气。他又扒了几下，把表层的湿土刮掉，露出下面相对干一些的土层，然后靠树坐下。
铁兴在他旁边坐下来，背靠着另一棵树干。两个人隔着大概两步的距离，都没有说话。

林子里不安静。虫鸣声一阵一阵的，偶尔有鸟扑棱棱地从树枝间飞过去，还有不知道什么小动物在落叶间窸窸窣窣地跑动。每一种声响都让人下意识地绷一下，然后过了好一会儿才松开。
苏尘靠着树干，眼睛盯着林子外面的那片月光。他没有睡意。不是不累——是身体里的气血还在翻涌。从血殷宗逃出来的那一系列动作——翻窗、放倒守卫、开暗门——都没有动用气，但之前和殷蕊那一夜的气血运转留下的影响还没有完全平下去。
他能感觉到体内的血气在动。不是激烈的动，是一种像暗流一样的动，贴着经脉的内壁慢慢地滑过去，带着微微的热度。
铁兴在那边动了动，换了个姿势。
“喂。”他的声音很低，低到刚好能听见。
苏尘“嗯”了一声。
“差点忘了。”铁兴说，“我一直没问你叫什么。”
苏尘沉默了一下。然后说：“苏尘。”
“苏尘。”铁兴重复了一遍这个名字，像是在嘴里过了一遍，然后说，“你是怎么活下来的？”
苏尘没有立刻回答。他听懂了铁兴的意思——不是问他逃出来这事，是问他怎么没死。在血殷宗的牢里待过两个月的人都知道，被带走的人没有能回来的。铁兴亲眼看着他被殷蕊选中，看着他被守卫押走，然后过了两天，这个人又活着回来了，还顺带把他救出来了。
苏尘沉默了一会儿。
“说不清楚。”他说，语气平淡，“反正没死成。”
铁兴等了一下，见他没下文了，啧了一声。
“行吧。反正活着就行。”他说，语气轻飘飘的，像是刚才那个问题本身也没多重要，随口一问罢了。他把嘴里的草茎换了个方向叼着，调整了一下靠树的姿势，“不然我刚认识个人就又没了，多没意思。”
夜风从树冠的缝隙里漏下来，吹在脸上，带着一股松脂的气味。苏尘闭上眼睛，没有睡着，只是让身体休息。
——
天亮之后，苏尘看清楚了周围的状况。
他们所在的是一片连绵的山岭，树木以松树和柞木为主，夹杂着大量的灌木和荆棘。山势不算陡，但地形复杂——沟壑纵横，到处都是被雨水冲刷出来的浅沟，沟里堆着碎石和断枝，走起来很费劲。
铁兴蹲在一条溪沟边，用手捧了水喝了一口，然后漱了漱口吐掉。
“这水能喝。”他说。

Chapter 51 Thousand Opportunities
The moonlight shone on the hillside, and the silvery white light illuminated the entire cemetery clearly. Su Chen and Tie Xing did not look back, stepping on weeds and gravel as they walked down. The stone wall behind him grew farther and farther under the moonlight, and was finally obscured by the ups and downs of the hillside and could no longer be seen.
There is no road underfoot.
It was all weeds and gravel. Every step was slippery, and every now and then I stepped on a loose stone. The stone rolled down, making a series of noises in the silent night. Su Chen tried his best to walk in places with dense grass - the soil in places with dense grass is firmer and less slippery. Tie Xing followed him, his steps heavier than his, and he could hear the sound of stones being ground into the soil with every step he took.
After going down the slope, there is a denser mountain forest ahead. The trees were not high, but very dense—pines, oaks, and shrubs, growing together in a mess, their branches intertwined, casting dark shadows in the moonlight. The fallen leaves on the ground were thick and soft when stepped on, emitting a damp smell of rotten wood.
Su Chen stood at the edge of the forest and looked back.
The stone wall on the hillside is no longer visible. The entire hillside was quiet under the moonlight, with only the sound of the wind blowing over the grass tips.
Tiexing stood next to him and looked back. His breathing hadn't completely calmed down yet, and his chest was rising and falling.
"We really came out," he said. There was a sense of unreality in his tone, as if he was still confirming that he was not dreaming.
"I haven't gone out yet," Su Chen said, "I just came out of the cave. I'm still on someone else's property."
Tiexing thought for a moment and nodded.
"Where to go?" he asked.
Su Chen raised his head and looked at the position of the moon. He stayed in the cave for several days, not knowing the direction outside, but the direction of the moon was always the same. He pointed to the northwest - the mountains there seemed lower and the trees were sparse, so it should be possible to climb over.
"Over there."
The two of them didn't say anything more, stepped on the fallen leaves, and went into the forest.
——
On the first night after being dug out of the graveyard, the two of them barely slept.
It's not that I don't want to sleep - it's that I simply can't find a place to lie down. The ground in the forest was uneven and full of protruding tree roots and stones buried under fallen leaves. It was very uncomfortable when I sat down, and even more uncomfortable when I lay down. Moreover, the mountain breeze at night was cold, blowing in through the gaps in the forest, bringing with it moisture, which quickly blew through the clothes.
Su Chen found a big pine tree with a thick trunk and an open crown like an umbrella, blocking most of the moonlight and night wind. He squatted down next to the root of the tree and used his hands to peel off the fallen leaves on the ground - underneath the fallen leaves was wet soil, with a strong earthy smell. He scraped a few more times to scrape off the wet soil on the surface, exposing the relatively dry soil below, and then sat down against the tree.
Tiexing sat down next to him, leaning against another tree trunk. The two people were about two steps apart and neither spoke.
The woods were not quiet. There were sounds of insects chirping, and occasionally birds fluttered between the branches, and unknown small animals rustled among the fallen leaves. Every sound made people tense up subconsciously, and then it took a while before they relaxed.
Su Chen leaned against the tree trunk and stared at the moonlight outside the forest. He was not sleepy. It's not that I'm not tired - it's that the blood in my body is still surging. The series of actions he took to escape from the Blood Yin Sect - climbing through the window, knocking down the guard, and opening the secret door - did not use Qi, but the impact of the previous night's Qi and blood circulation with Yin Rui has not completely subsided.
He could feel the blood moving in his body. It's not a violent movement, it's a movement like an undercurrent, sliding slowly against the inner wall of the meridians, with a slight heat.
Tiexing moved there and changed his posture.
"Hello." His voice was low, just low enough to be heard.
Su Chen said "hmm".
"I almost forgot." Tie Xing said, "II never asked you what your name was. "
Su Chen was silent for a moment. Then he said: "Su Chen. "
"Su Chen. "Tie Xing repeated the name, as if he had passed it through his mouth, and then said, "How did you survive? "
Su Chen didn't answer immediately. He understood what Tie Xing meant - he wasn't asking about his escape, but why he wasn't dead. Anyone who has spent two months in Xueyin Zong's prison knows that no one who is taken away can come back. Tie Xing personally watched him being selected by Yin Rui and saw him being taken away by the guards. Then two days later, the man came back alive and rescued him by the way.
Su Chen was silent for a while.
"Can't tell. "He said in a calm tone, "Anyway, I didn't die. "
Tie Xing waited for a moment, and when he saw that he had nothing to say, he clicked his tongue.
"Okay. Just stay alive anyway. " He said in a light tone, as if the question itself was not that important and was just asked casually. He changed the direction of the grass stem in his mouth and adjusted his posture against the tree. "Otherwise, I just met someone and then disappeared again. It would be boring. "
The night wind leaked through the gaps in the canopy of the trees and blew on my face, carrying a smell of pine resin. Su Chen closed his eyes, not falling asleep, but just letting his body rest.
——
After dawn, Su Chen saw the surrounding situation clearly.
They were in a continuous mountain range with trees mainly composed of pine and oak trees, mixed with a large number of shrubs and thorns. The mountain is not steep, but the terrain is complex - ravines are crisscrossed, and there are shallow ditches washed out by rain everywhere. The ditches are filled with gravel and broken branches, making walking very difficult.
Tiexing squatted by a creek, took a sip of water with his hand, then rinsed his mouth and spit it out.
"This water is drinkable. " he said.
